definition: Grouping time series by shape or dynamics without labels — using elastic distances or learned representations.
details: Grouping time series by shape or dynamics without labels — using elastic distances or learned representations.

explainer.lead: Time series clustering groups series by shape or dynamics without labels. It matters for discovering structure in unlabelled temporal data where no ground-truth categories exist.

tiers.eli5: It is like sorting a pile of stock charts into groups by their overall shape, without anyone telling you what the groups should be.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers cluster series using elastic distances that tolerate shifts and warping, or by first learning an embedding of the series. A common pitfall is measuring distance poorly, so similar shapes land in different clusters.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, it partitions a set of series into groups so that within-group distance is low and between-group distance is high, where distance may be an elastic measure or a distance in a learned representation space. Limits: results depend heavily on the chosen distance and on normalisation of the series.

explainer.example: Unlabelled sensor traces can be sorted into piles by how their curves move over time, without any predefined category names.
